title.en: Zakariyya's Prayer and the Silent Sign of Yahya
title.zh: 宰凱里亞的祈禱與啞默之兆

region.en: Jerusalem Temple, mihrab of prayer (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 耶路撒冷聖殿祈禱壁龕（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs Ali 'Imran 3:38-41, Maryam 19:2-15; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 3:38-41 and 19:2-15

summary.en: Zakariyya prays: 'O my Lord, give me from Thee a good successor, for Thou art the Hearer of prayer.' The angels call him as he stands praying in the sanctuary: 'God announces to thee Yahya, who shall confirm the word of God.' 'Lord, how shall I have a son when age hath overtaken me, and my wife is barren?' — 'Thus God doth what He pleaseth.' He asks for a sign; the sign is that for three days he shall speak to no man. And God gives him Yahya: 'O Yahya, take the Book with firm purpose' — a devout Lord, chaste, and a prophet of the just.
summary.zh: 宰凱里亞在聖堂祈禱：『主啊，賜我一個善良的繼承者。』天使呼喚他：『主向你報喜——葉海雅，他將證實真主的言語。』『我妻已絕育，我已年邁，怎會得子？』——『主如此命其所欲。』他求徵兆；徵兆是三日不與人言。主賜其葉海雅：『葉海雅啊，當受持經書，意向堅定』——是貞潔的、敬畏的、正直的先知。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: When Zakariyya cried to his Lord, 'O my Lord, leave me not childless; but Thou art the best of heirs.' And We heard him: and We gave him John; and we made his wife right-fitting. Verily they were hasty in coming to good works, and called on Us with love and fear, and were humbled before Us.

And when he stood up in the sanctuary praying, the angels of God called him and said, 'God announceth to thee Yahya, who shall confirm the Word from God, a prince and chaste, and a prophet, and righteous one of the just.' He said, 'Lord! how shall I have a son, when age hath overtaken me, and my wife is barren?' He said, 'Thus doth God what pleaseth Him.' He said, 'Give me a token, then.' He said, 'The token shall be, that for three days thou shalt speak to no man except by signs.'

O Yahya, take the Book with firm purpose. And We bestowed on him wisdom when a child, and a tenderness from Ourself, and purity; and he was devout and kind to his parents; and he was not a rebellious, wicked person. And peace was on him on the day he was born, and the day of his death, and the day when he shall be raised to life.

title.en: The Angels Speak to Maryam: 'God Chooseth Thee'
title.zh: 天使對麥爾彥說話：『主揀選了你』

region.en: Nazareth / Jerusalem temple (symbolic pin at Jerusalem)
region.zh: 拿撒勒／耶路撒冷聖殿（象徵性定位於耶路撒冷）

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs Ali 'Imran 3:42-47, Maryam 19:16-26; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 3:42-47

summary.en: The angels say to Maryam: 'God hath chosen thee, and made thee pure, and raised thee above all women of the worlds; worship thy Lord, bow thyself down, and adore.' She is told of a Word from Him, Isa the Messiah — 'She said, How shall I have a son whom man hath not touched?' — 'Thus God createth what He pleaseth.' In the withdrawal she meets a spirit in the form of a perfect man: 'I am the messenger of thy Lord, that I may give thee a gift, a faultless boy.'
summary.zh: 天使對麥爾彥說：『主揀選了你，使你純潔，並提拔你超越世界萬民之女；當敬拜你的主。』她被告知主的言語——麥西哈爾撒：『未曾有人觸碰我，我怎會得子？』——『主如此造其所欲者。』她退居時遇一化身完美之人的精靈：『我是你主的使者，將賜你一個無瑕疵的男孩。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; presented via public-domain translation; the Qur'anic virgin birth narrative differs from Christian Gospel accounts.

passages.text: And remember when the angel said, 'O Maryam, verily hath God chosen thee, and purified thee, and chosen thee above the women of the worlds: worship thy Lord, bow thyself down, and adore.' This is one of the announcements of things unseen, which We reveal to thee; for thou wast not with them when they cast their lots with pens, which of them should rear Maryam; nor wast thou with them when they disputed about it.

When the angels said, 'O Maryam, God announceth to thee the Word from Himself: his name shall be, Messiah, Jesus, the son of Maryam, illustrious in this world and in the next, and of those who are near the presence of God. And he shall speak to men when in the cradle, and in maturity, and shall be one of the just.' She said, 'Lord! how shall I have a son, when man hath not touched me?' He said, 'Thus: God will create what He pleaseth: when He decreeth a thing, He only saith Be, and it is.'

And make mention of Maryam in the Book; when she went apart from her family, eastward, and took a veil to screen herself from them; and We sent Our spirit to her, and he appeared to her in the shape of a perfect man. She said, 'I fly for refuge unto the God of Mercy from thee; if thou fearest Him, begone from me, and approach me not.' He answered, 'I am only a messenger of thy Lord, that I may bestow on thee a boy most pure.'

title.en: Under the Palm: Isa Speaks in the Cradle
title.zh: 棕櫚樹下：爾撒搖籃中說話

region.en: Bethlehem / palm grove outside the city (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 伯利恆／城外棕櫚林（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah Maryam 19:22-35; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 19:22-35

summary.en: She withdrew with him to a distant place; the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm: 'Would that I had died before this.' A voice from beneath her: 'Grieve not: thy Lord hath provided a rivulet; shake the trunk of the palm and it shall let fall fresh ripe dates; eat and drink, and thine eye be refreshed.' To her people she comes with the child; they charge her. 'I am the servant of God; He hath given me the Book, and made me a prophet: He hath blessed me wheresoever I am, and hath enjoined on me prayer and the poor-rate, so long as I shall live; and to be dutiful to her that beareth me.' 'Peace was on me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I shall be raised to life.'
summary.zh: 她攜子退至遠處；分娩之痛使她靠向棕櫚樹幹：『恨不得我早死了。』樹下有聲呼喚：『勿憂傷；你的主已在下面造出溪流；搖動棕櫚樹幹，必落下鮮熟之椰棗；可吃可飲，眼目舒適。』她抱子至族人前，被責問。『我是真主的僕人：他賜我經典，立我為先知；並命我禮拜施捨，孝敬生我之母。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And she went in private with him to a distant place; and the pains of childbirth came upon her near the trunk of the palm, and she said, 'Would to God I had died before this, and had been a thing forgotten, forgotten of all!' And a voice from beneath her cried to her, 'Grieve not, for thy Lord hath provided a rivulet beneath thee; and shake the trunk of the palm-tree towards thee, and it shall drop fresh ripe dates upon thee. Eat therefore and drink, and thine eye shall be refreshed; and if thou seest any man, say, I have vowed abstinence to the God of Mercy: this day I will not speak with any man.'

And she came to her people with him in her bosom. Said they, 'O Maryam, now hast thou done a strange thing: O sister of Aaron, thy father was not a wicked man, neither was thy mother a woman of shame.' And she pointed to the child; but they answered, 'How shall we talk with him who is a child in the cradle?'

And the child said, 'Verily I am the servant of God; He hath given me the Book, and made me a prophet: and He hath made me blessed, wheresoever I may be; and He hath enjoined on me prayer and alms-giving, so long as I shall live; and to be dutiful to her that bare me; and hath not made me proud, insolent. And the peace of God was on me the day I was born, and will be the day of my death, and the day when I shall be raised to life. This is Jesus, the son of Mary: this is the truth of which ye are doubtless in doubt.'

title.en: The Table Sent Down to Isa

region.en: Galilee, table of the apostles (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 加利利使徒宴桌（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah al-Ma'idah 5:112-115; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 5:112-115

summary.en: The apostles say: 'O Isa, son of Maryam! can thy Lord send down a table to us from heaven?' He answers: 'Fear God, if ye are believers.' They press — 'We wish to eat thereof, and that our hearts may be assured, and that we may know that thou hast told us the truth.' Isa prays: 'O God our Lord, send down to us from heaven a table, that there may be a festival to the first of us and to the last, and a sign from Thee; and give us means of subsistence, for Thou art the best of providers.' God says: 'I will send it down; but whoever among you shall disbelieve after, I will chastise him with a chastisement wherewith I have chastised no other creature.'
summary.zh: 使徒說：『爾撒啊，你的主能否從天上降下宴桌給我們？』他答：『你們當敬畏主，若你們是信士。』他們堅請——『我們想吃了，使我們的心得定，使我們知道你告訴了我們真理。』爾撒祈禱：『主啊，求你從天上降下宴桌，作為前後眾人的節日，從你而來的蹟象。』主說：『我必降下；但此後不信者，我必以從未懲罰過任何生靈之刑懲之。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation; the surah is named 'The Table' for this episode.

passages.text: Remember when the apostles said, 'O Isa, son of Maryam! can thy Lord send down to us a table furnished from heaven?' He said, 'Fear God if ye are believers.' They said, 'We wish to eat thereof, and that our hearts may be at rest, and that we may know that thou hast told us the truth, and that we may be witnesses of it.' Said Isa, the son of Maryam, 'O God our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven, that it may become a festival to us, to the first of us and to the last of us, and a sign from Thee; and give us means of subsistence, for Thou art the best of providers.' And God said, 'Verily I will cause it to descend upon you; and whoever among you believeth not, I will chastise him with a chastisement with which I have chastised no other creature in all the world.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 5:112-114 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim. / Paraphrase of Qur'an 5:115 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.

title.en: The Crucifixion Reframed: 'They Did Not Slay Him'
title.zh: 十字架之重構：『他們未曾殺他』

region.en: Jerusalem, place of the crucifixion (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 耶路撒冷受難地（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah an-Nisa 4:156-159; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 4:156-159

summary.en: Their saying: 'We have put to death the Messiah, Jesus the son of Mary, the apostle of God.' But they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; but he was represented to them as such: and they who disagree concerning him are in doubt; they have no knowledge concerning him, but follow only probable conjecture; and they did not surely kill him — but God took him up to Himself. And there shall be none of the people of the Book but shall believe in him before his death.
summary.zh: 他們說：『我們確已殺害麥西哈爾撒——麥爾彥之子、真主的使者。』他們未曾殺他，也未把他釘十字架上，但他們以為如此；對他有所爭執的人，都陷於疑惑之中——他們不過憑猜測，確未殺他。真主已把他擢升到自己那裡；信奉天經的人，在他死去之前，都必定信他。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; a doctrinally central divergence from Christian accounts; presented as text, not as a religious claim; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And because of their unbelief and their strong imputing to Maryam a terrible falsehood, and their saying, 'We have slain the Messiah, Jesus the son of Maryam, the apostle of God.' Yet they slew him not, and they crucified him not, but he was represented to them as such; and they who differed concerning him were in doubt: they had no certain knowledge of him, but only followed an opinion; and they did not really kill him. But God took him up to Himself: and God is mighty and wise. And there shall be none of the people of the Book, but shall believe in him before his death: and on the day of resurrection he shall be a witness against them.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 4:156-158 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim. / Paraphrase of Qur'an 4:159 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.

title.en: Yunus and the Fish: Three Lamps in Darkness
title.zh: 優努斯與大魚：幽暗中的三重黑暗

region.en: Open sea near Nineveh (symbolic pin at Mosul)
region.zh: 尼尼微附近海域（象徵性定位於摩蘇爾）

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs 21:87-88, 37:139-148, 10:98; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Suras 21, 37, 10

summary.en: Dhun-Nun flees like a slave into a laden ship; lots are cast and he is of the losers; the fish swallows him. In the triple darkness — of the sea, of the fish, of the night — he cries: 'There is no God but Thou: glory be to Thee: I have done evil.' 'We heard him and delivered him from his grief; and thus do We deliver the faithful.' And God cast him on the dry land; and he had passed by a hundred thousand, or more, of his people: and they believed, and We gave them the enjoyment of this life.
summary.zh: 帶魚的優努斯如奴僕般逃入滿載之船；拈鬮他被中；大魚吞之。三重黑暗——海、魚、夜——他呼喊：『除你外，別無神明；榮耀歸你；我實行不義。』『我們應答他，救他脫離憂患；我如此拯救信士。』主使登岸，並經過他的十萬或更多的族人：他們歸信，我賜他們享受。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation; Jonah is the only prophet to whom a whole surah is not named but appears in the Qur'an with a whole sura named after him.

passages.text: And Dzunnun fled like a runaway slave, and went on board a ship fully laden, and they drew lots, and he was of the losers; and the fish swallowed him, and he was worthy of blame. Had he not been of those who glorify God, he had remained in its belly until the day when men shall be raised from the dead.

And Yunus, remember him, when he went away in anger and supposed We had no power over him; and he cried out in darkness, 'There is no God but Thou: glory be to Thee! I have done amiss.' So We heard him and delivered him from his grief, and thus do We deliver the faithful. And We cast him on the bare shore, and he was sick; and We caused a gourd-tree to grow up over him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 21:87-88 and 37:145-146 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.

passages.text: And We sent him on a mission to a hundred thousand men, or to a greater number; and they believed, and We gave them the enjoyment of this life for a season. Why hath there not been one city, which on its believing might have reaped the blessing of its faith? — the people of Yunus believed not until they had seen a grievous chastisement; and only Jonah was an exception.

title.en: Ayyub: The Cry of the Afflicted and the Fountain
title.zh: 安優卜：受苦者的呼喊與泉水

region.zh: 烏茲地／浩蘭（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs 21:83-84, 38:41-44; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Suras 21:83-84 and 38:41-44

summary.en: Ayyub cries to his Lord: 'Evil hath touched me; and Thou art the most merciful of the merciful.' 'We heard him and relieved him of the evil which was on him; and We restored to him his family, and, with them, others of his race, in mercy from Us and a warning to those who serve Us.' And remember Our servant Ayyub, when he cried to his Lord, 'Satan hath touched me with labour and suffering.' 'Strike the earth with thy foot: here is a wash to drink, and cool to bathe in.' And We gave him his family, and the like of them with them — a mercy from Us, and a warning to the understanding.
summary.zh: 安優卜呼其主：『災害已觸及我；你是最慈的施恩者。』『我們應答他，除去其身上的災害；並賜還其家眷，且加以同類者——出於我的恩慈，也是侍奉者的記念。』又念僕人安優卜：『魔鬼以勞苦與災害加於我。』『你用腳踏地：這裡有洗滌的涼水可浴。』我賜還其家眷，並加以同類者——這是我的恩慈，是有悟者的記念。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation; the tafsir tradition fills the Qur'anic brevity with the length of Job's affliction.

passages.text: And remember Our servant Ayyub, when he cried to his Lord, 'The evil one hath touched me with toil and weariness.' We said, 'Strike the earth with thy foot: here is a wash to drink, and cool to bathe in.' And We gave him his family, and the like of them with them, in Our mercy, and as a memorial to men of understanding.

And Ayyub cried to his Lord, 'Evil hath afflicted me, and Thou art the most merciful of the merciful.' And We heard him, and relieved him of the evil under which he laboured; and We restored to him his family, and doubled their number in Our mercy, and as a warning to those who serve Us. And take in thy hand a bundle of rushes and strike therewith, and thou shalt not violate thine oath; for We found him patient: an excellent servant shall he be; for he turned himself towards Us.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 21:83-84 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim. / Paraphrase of Qur'an 38:44 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.

title.en: Idris: We Raised Him to a High Station
title.zh: 易德里斯：主把他擢升到高處

region.en: Land of the antediluvian prophets (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 洪水前諸先知之地（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs Maryam 19:56-57, al-Anbiya 21:85-86; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 19:56-57

summary.en: Make mention of Idris in the Book; he was a just man and a prophet, and We raised him to a high place. And Ishmael, and Idris, and Dhul-Kifl — all were of the patient: and We made them enter into Our mercy, for they were of the righteous.
summary.zh: 在經中提及易德里斯；他是正直者，是先知；我把他擢升到一個高處。並易司馬儀、易德里斯、左勒蓋爾菲爾——他們都是堅忍者；我使他們進入我的恩慈，因為他們是正直者。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; Idris is identified with Enoch in the tafsir tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And make a mention of Idris in the Book; he was a just person and a prophet; and We took him up into a high place. And we said, 'O Idris, enter into the mercy of thy Lord.' And remember Ishmael, and Idris, and Dhul-Kifl: all were of the patient: and We made them enter into Our mercy, for they were of the righteous.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Qur'an 19:56-57 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim. / Paraphrase of Qur'an 21:85-86 (Rodwell 1861); not verbatim.

region.en: Mecca, year of the Elephant (literal pin)

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah al-Fil 105 (Meccan, among the earliest); Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 105

summary.en: Hast thou not seen how thy Lord dealt with the army of the Elephant? Did He not confuse their plans, and turn them into dust-wind? And He sent against them birds in flocks, clay-stones of baked earth, which He cast upon them: and He made them like stubble eaten by cattle.
summary.zh: 你豈未見你的主怎樣處理象軍？他破壞他們的計謀，化為糠粃；並遣群鳥襲之，投以燒結的陶土之石，使眾人如被嚼的草料。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; this is the episode that sets the year of Muhammad's birth; public-domain translation.

passages.text: Hast thou not seen how thy Lord dealt with the army of the Elephant? Did He not make their design go wrong? And He sent against them birds in flocks; clay-stones of baked earth, which He cast upon them; and He made them like stubble eaten by cattle.

title.en: Haman's Tower to Reach the God of Musa
title.zh: 哈曼的高塔：欲登穆薩之神

region.en: Egypt, mud-brick tower of Pharaoh (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 埃及法老的泥磚高塔（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs 28:38, 40:36-37; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Suras 28:38 and 40:36-37

summary.en: Pharaoh says: 'O nobles, I know not that ye have any god beside me: light a fire for me, O Haman, to bake clay, and build me a tower, that I may mount up to the god of Moses, for verily I think him a liar.' And the arrogant designs of Pharaoh in the land, and his perversion of justice, are those on whom God sets the evil; 'O Haman, build me a tower, that I may reach the highways — the highways of the heavens, that I may look upon the God of Moses; for verily I think him a liar.' Thus is made fair-seeming to Pharaoh the evil of his deeds, and he is turned from the way; and the designs of Pharaoh end only in loss.
summary.zh: 法老說：『眾卿啊，除我外，我不知你們另有神明；哈曼啊，為我點火燒磚，為我築一高塔，好登穆薩之神那裡——我認他是撒謊者。』並法老在國中的暴行與偏私——真主使之自負其罪；『哈曼啊，為我築塔，使我達到天路，去看穆薩之神。』法老惡行被美化，被誘離正道；法老的計謀終歸滅亡。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation; the tower episode parallels the Babel legend and is unique to the Qur'anic Haman.

passages.text: And Pharaoh said, 'O nobles, I know not that ye have any god besides me: light me a fire, O Haman, to bake clay, and build me a tower, that I may mount up to the god of Moses, for verily I think that he is of the liars.' And the arrogance which Pharaoh and his host practised in the land, and his perversion of justice, is that on which God shall set the evil.

And Pharaoh said, 'O Haman, build me a tower, that I may reach the pathways — the pathways of the heavens — that I may look upon the God of Moses, for verily I think him to be a liar.' And thus was made fair-seeming to Pharaoh the evil of his deeds, and he was turned away from the path of God: and the designs of Pharaoh led only to ruin.

title.en: The Believer of the City's Farthest Quarter

region.en: Unnamed city of the warned (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 被警告的無名之城（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah Ya-Sin 36:13-29; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 36:13-29

summary.en: We send two warners, and they charge them with falsehood; then We send a third, and they say, 'Verily we are sent to you.' 'Ye are only men like ourselves.' 'The God of Mercy hath sent us — obey us.' They accuse them of augury; and a man comes running from the farthest part of the city: 'O my people, believe the messengers.' The people answer that they will surely stone them; the believer asks that he be raised among the righteous — 'Enter thou Paradise! He said, Would that men knew what my Lord hath forgiven me, and hath made me one of the honoured!'
summary.zh: 主遣二使者警誡，反遭斥為謊者；再遣第三位，說：『我們確被遣於你們。』『你們不過與我們相同的人。』『至慈的主遣我們——當順從我們。』人們斥為兇兆；一男子自城中最遠之處跑來：『我的族人啊，當信使者。』人們欲投石；歸信者求立於善人之中——『入樂園吧！』他說：『但願人們知道，我的主赦了我，並使我成為榮貴者。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; the 'believer of Ya-Sin' is a favourite qisas figure; public-domain translation.

passages.text: Set forth to them as an example the inhabitants of the city, when the apostles came to it. When We sent two apostles to them and they charged them with imposture, We reinforced them with a third; and they said, 'We are sent to you of God.' They said, 'Ye are but men like us; the God of Mercy hath not sent anything: ye do nothing but lie.' They said, 'Our Lord knoweth that we are sent on a mission to you: and our duty is only plain preaching.' The inhabitants said, 'We augur evil from you: if ye desist not, we will surely stone you, and a grievous punishment shall ye receive from us.'

They said, 'Your augury is with yourselves: if ye be warned, will ye be warned? Ye are a headstrong people.' And a man came running from the farthest part of the city, and said, 'O my people, believe the apostles: believe him who is not solicitous to be rewarded.' The people said, 'We forebode evil from you: if ye cease not, we will stone you, and a grievous punishment shall befall you at our hands.'

It was said to the believer, 'Enter thou into the Garden.' He said, 'Would to God that my people had known of that for which my Lord hath forgiven me, and hath made me one of the honoured!' And after him We did not send down any host from heaven upon his people, nor was it meet that We should.
